sentence: From the sofa nobody can tell which row is selected on the living-room screen.

reviewer_notes.what_the_code_does_now: TVButtonStyle: focus = 4 pt white ring + scale 1.04 (wide/cards) or 1.08 (icons) + shadow; background surface #1A1F29 -> surfaceRaised #242B38 (approx 1.4:1 between the two states). CardRail cards: ring drawn on the 400x225 artwork only, no fill change, rail heading never changes. TextTileRail tiles use the same style. Nothing marks which RAIL (row) holds focus: headings of all rails stay textPrimary, unfocused rails are not dimmed. Selected tab in CatalogueShell is the system TabView.
reviewer_notes.what_a_good_answer_says: On TV 'selected' = focused. The focused item must read from 3 m: ring/lift/fill change with high contrast (ring >= 3:1 vs surroundings and thick enough to survive scaling down to a 10-foot view), the focused row itself must be distinguishable (row heading emphasis or dimming of non-focused rows), keep the ring with Reduce Motion, keep colour not the only cue, keep within the 60 pt safe margin / 48 pt overscan limit when lifting, and keep selected (checkmark) distinct from focused where both exist (track picker, tabs). Must not talk about hover, touch targets, breakpoints or mouse/keyboard focus rings for the web.
reviewer_notes.screen_in_scope: CatalogueShell (Watch tab: ContinueWatchingView; Search tab: CardRail / TextTileRail rails) and the shared TVButtonStyle. Player/sign-in only insofar as the shared style changes.
